headline: Price, Van Veen and Ross Smith out on a Minehead night of shocks
standfirst: Four seeds went in the evening session at Butlins, and Michael Smith found the sort of form he has been missing for years.
body: The favourites have to come through Friday night at Minehead, and a lot of them did not. Henry Coates beat Wessel Nijman despite a 110.56 average, and Sebastian Bialecki ended Gerwyn Price's perfect record against him with a 6-4 win. Those two have their own reports. The rest of the night was just as odd.

Gian van Veen, the world number two, lost 6-4 to Jeffrey De Graaf, ranked 41st. The averages were 91.66 to 91.18, which says it all: nobody took the match by the throat, and De Graaf was the one still standing at the end. Ross Smith, sixth in the world, went out 6-3 to Michael Smith, ranked 37th, who averaged 99.26 against 90.05. It was a long way from the form he has shown on TV lately.

There was more. Mickey Mansell came from behind to beat Rob Cross 6-5 in a deciding leg. Stephen Bunting needed a decider to get past Max Hopp 6-5. Jermaine Wattimena edged Keane Barry by the same score, and Krzysztof Ratajski averaged 102.92 and still lost 6-4 to Damon Heta, who now meets Luke Humphries.

The big names who did survive were not cruising. Michael van Gerwen beat Connor Scutt 6-3 with an average of 89.35, and Humphries saw off Darryl Pilgrim 6-3 averaging 93.32. Beau Greaves won her debut, 6-3 against Christian Kist, with an 89.63 average to his 86.44. Ryan Searle thrashed Brendan Dolan 6-1, and Darius Labanauskas beat Cristo Reyes by the same scoreline.
Our view: Michael Smith is the story to follow. A 99 average and a draw that suddenly looks open is exactly what this tournament needed.
